title: Finding
description: The triage report a gke-triage specialist returns for one incident. One finding per affected object: if a diagnosis covers several pods, the coordinator dispatches several specialists rather than the specialist listing them here.

severity.description: critical = must fix now (down, crashlooping, OOMKilled); warning = fix soon (missing probes, no PDB, :latest images); info = an optimization opportunity, not an outage.

title.description: Short headline naming the object and the problem, e.g. 'CrashLoopBackOff on api-7d9f8b6c4-xk2p1'.

detail.description: The diagnosis: what is wrong, which evidence says so, and why. Name the resources and the values you read.

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace of the affected object. Empty for cluster-scoped findings.

kind.description: Kubernetes kind of the affected object, capitalized and singular: Pod, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Node, Job, CronJob, Service, PersistentVolume, Namespace. Empty only for cluster-wide observations.

resource_name.description: Name of the single affected object, exactly as it appears in the cluster.

reason.description: Stable machine-style cause in CamelCase — CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, NodeNotReady, MissingResourceLimits. Reuse the same token for the same class of problem across runs; do not reword it.

recommended_actions.description: Concrete, ordered next steps in prose, for a human reader. Nothing here is executed — prose cannot be approved, only read. If a step is something this workload can actually do, say it again in proposed_change.

proposed_change.description: The executable form of your recommendation: the exact calls an operator would approve. Every entry must name a tool from this workload's tool_catalog and carry that tool's own arguments; both are checked when you return, and a report naming a tool that does not exist, or arguments that do not fit its schema, is refused back to you. Send an empty list when you cannot name an exact call — that is a complete, valid report, and it is the right answer for a diagnosis that needs a human decision, a bigger change than triage covers, or a tool this workload was not given. Never invent a plausible-looking call to fill the field.

tool.description: Name of the tool to call, exactly as the tool_catalog spells it.

arguments.description: That tool's arguments as a JSON object, encoded in a string — for example "{\"namespace\":\"prod\",\"name\":\"api\"}". Send "{}" for a tool that takes none. A string, not an object, because the arguments differ per tool and this schema cannot declare their keys in advance.

escalate.description: True when the fix is not a triage-scope action — a bigger node pool, a suspected memory leak, an app-team bug. Say why in detail.
